commit_message:
fix(dispatch-creation): register enum literals for parsing data-tiling hint op types

The CLI option that lists op families eligible for data-tiling annotation
takes `EncodingOpType` enum values, but no `cl::values` were registered for
it. Hence, passing a keyword such as `convolution` on the command line failed
to parse. Register the literals (`matmul`, `scaled_matmul`, `convolution`)
so the option is actually usable from `iree-compile`.

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

The CLI option that lists op families eligible for data-tiling annotation
takes `EncodingOpType` enum values, but no `cl::values` were registered for
it. Hence, passing a keyword such as `convolution` on the command line failed
to parse. Register the literals (`matmul`, `scaled_matmul`, `convolution`)
so the option is actually usable from `iree-compile`.

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: runtime_tracing :: ubuntu-24.04-arm :: tracy

fix(dispatch-creation): register enum literals for parsing data-tiling hint op types

The CLI option that lists op families eligible for data-tiling annotation
takes `EncodingOpType` enum values, but no `cl::values` were registered for
it. Hence, passing a keyword such as `convolution` on the command line failed
to parse. Register the literals (`matmul`, `scaled_matmul`, `convolution`)
so the option is actually usable from `iree-compile`.

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Util] Fix 32-bit wrap of util.string.format placeholder-count check

parseFormatString computes expectedArgCount = maxArgIndex + 1 in 32-bit.
For an explicit placeholder near UINT_MAX (e.g. "{4294967295}") this wraps to
0, so the op verifies with zero operands, and StringFormatOp::fold then reads
argStrings[4294967295] on an empty vector (OOB). Compute the count in 64-bit
in both copies of parseFormatString (verifier and folder) so the out-of-range
placeholder is rejected at verification.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

fix(dispatch-creation): register enum literals for parsing data-tiling hint op types

it. Hence, passing a keyword such as `convolution` on the command line failed
to parse. Register the literals (`matmul`, `scaled_matmul`, `convolution`)
so the option is actually usable from `iree-compile`.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add SME lowering-strategy tests for f64 and unsupported i8 matmuls (#24656)

`getMatmulAArch64SMEVectorSizes` (within `KernelDispatch.cpp`) only had
test coverage for the f32 matmul case.

This PR add two tests:
- `f64` which uses `[4]x[8]` SME tiles instead of the `[8]x[8]` used for
f32.

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/50d0addfb49254e0b7b746959b360c79437281cc/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMCPU/KernelDispatch.cpp#L1465-L1471
- `i8` which SME does not support

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/50d0addfb49254e0b7b746959b360c79437281cc/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMCPU/KernelDispatch.cpp#L1488-L1502

_AI disclaimer_: I used `Claude:Sonnet5` to write the checks.

---------

Signed-off-by: Federico Bruzzone <federico.bruzzone.i@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[LLVMCPU] Add SME lowering-strategy tests for f64 and unsupported i8 matmuls (#24656)

`getMatmulAArch64SMEVectorSizes` (within `KernelDispatch.cpp`) only had
test coverage for the f32 matmul case.

This PR add two tests:
- `f64` which uses `[4]x[8]` SME tiles instead of the `[8]x[8]` used for
f32.

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/50d0addfb49254e0b7b746959b360c79437281cc/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMCPU/KernelDispatch.cpp#L1465-L1471
- `i8` which SME does not support

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/50d0addfb49254e0b7b746959b360c79437281cc/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMCPU/KernelDispatch.cpp#L1488-L1502

_AI disclaimer_: I used `Claude:Sonnet5` to write the checks.

[LLVMCPU] Add SME lowering-strategy tests for f64 and unsupported i8 matmuls (#24656)

`getMatmulAArch64SMEVectorSizes` (within `KernelDispatch.cpp`) only had
test coverage for the f32 matmul case.

This PR add two tests:
- `f64` which uses `[4]x[8]` SME tiles instead of the `[8]x[8]` used for
f32.

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/50d0addfb49254e0b7b746959b360c79437281cc/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMCPU/KernelDispatch.cpp#L1465-L1471

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/50d0addfb49254e0b7b746959b360c79437281cc/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMCPU/KernelDispatch.cpp#L1488-L1502

_AI disclaimer_: I used `Claude:Sonnet5` to write the checks.

commit_message:
[Stream] Bounds-check tied operand index in verifyTiedOperandEncodings (#24686)

## Summary
Bounds-check the tied-operand index in `verifyTiedOperandEncodings` so
an out-of-range `tied_operands` value is reported as a verification
error instead of indexing the operand-encodings array out of bounds.

## Context
`verifyTiedOperandEncodings` (used by tied stream ops such as
`stream.tensor.dispatch`) walks each result's tied operand and compares
`operandEncodings[operandIndex]` against the result encoding.
`operandIndex` is derived from the op's `tied_operands` attribute.

## Problem
The `tied_operands` value is not range-checked for this op before the
encoding lookup, so an index beyond the operand count reads
`operandEncodings` out of bounds. Such an index is reachable through the
generic assembly form (which bypasses the op's custom-format checks) —
for example, a dispatch with a single operand encoding but a
`tied_operands` entry pointing at operand 5:
```mlir
%0 = "stream.tensor.dispatch"(...) {
  tied_operands = array<i64: 5>, ...
} : (...) -> ...
```
`operandIndex` (5) then indexes the single-element `operandEncodings`
out of bounds during verification.

## Fix
If `operandIndex >= operandEncodings.size()`, emit a verification error
(`tied operand index N is out of range of the M operand encoding(s)`)
instead of indexing out of bounds.

---

(Claude) and reviewed before submission.

---------

name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[Stream] Bounds-check tied operand index in verifyTiedOperandEncodings (#24686)

## Summary
Bounds-check the tied-operand index in `verifyTiedOperandEncodings` so
an out-of-range `tied_operands` value is reported as a verification
error instead of indexing the operand-encodings array out of bounds.

## Context
`verifyTiedOperandEncodings` (used by tied stream ops such as
`stream.tensor.dispatch`) walks each result's tied operand and compares
`operandEncodings[operandIndex]` against the result encoding.
`operandIndex` is derived from the op's `tied_operands` attribute.

## Problem
The `tied_operands` value is not range-checked for this op before the
encoding lookup, so an index beyond the operand count reads
`operandEncodings` out of bounds. Such an index is reachable through the
generic assembly form (which bypasses the op's custom-format checks) —
for example, a dispatch with a single operand encoding but a
`tied_operands` entry pointing at operand 5:
```mlir
%0 = "stream.tensor.dispatch"(...) {
  tied_operands = array<i64: 5>, ...
} : (...) -> ...
```
`operandIndex` (5) then indexes the single-element `operandEncodings`
out of bounds during verification.

## Fix
If `operandIndex >= operandEncodings.size()`, emit a verification error
(`tied operand index N is out of range of the M operand encoding(s)`)
instead of indexing out of bounds.

(Claude) and reviewed before submission.

[DispatchCreation] Register enum literals for parsing data-tiling hint op types (#24711)

The CLI option that lists op families eligible for data-tiling
annotation takes `EncodingOpType` enum values, but no `cl::values` were
registered for it. Hence, passing a keyword such as `convolution` on the
command line to
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` failed to
parse. Register the literals (`matmul`, `scaled_matmul`, `convolution`)
so the option is actually usable from `iree-compile`.
